## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is identified with an uncle of Muhammad, his wife is given a name, and the occasion of the passage is told in later works.
- Hadith to add later: reports about the occasion of the passage, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Abu Lahab and his wife  (`#abu-lahab-and-his-wife`)

Cited ayat: 111:1-5

> **111:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِى لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
>
> **111:2** مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ
>
> **111:3** سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
>
> **111:4** وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ
>
> **111:5** فِى جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍۭ

### Claims

**c1** (111:1): The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished.

**c2** (111:2): His wealth and what he earned did not avail him.

**c3** (111:3): He will burn in a fire of flame.

**c4** (111:4): His wife is mentioned as the carrier of firewood.

**c5** (111:5): Her neck has a rope of palm fibre around it.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished [c1]. His wealth and what he earned did not avail him [c2]. It says that he will burn in a fire of flame, and it mentions his wife as the carrier of firewood [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished [c1]. His wealth and what he earned did not avail him [c2]. He will burn in a fire of flame [c3]. His wife is mentioned as the carrier of firewood [c4]. Her neck has a rope of palm fibre around it [c5].

### Deep study

The passage names him as Abu Lahab and gives no other name [c1]. It speaks of his wife in the last ayat, and the ayat do not say what the carrier of firewood refers to [c4][c5].

### Kids mode

The Quran says that Abu Lahab's wealth and what he earned did not help him [c2]. His wife is called the carrier of firewood [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage says wealth and earnings did not avail him [c2]. Another is that the passage speaks of his wife as well as of him [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established in these ayat: who Abu Lahab was, what his own name was, or why he is named in this way. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is identified as an uncle of Muhammad, and his own name is given as Abd al-Uzza.
- Not established: the wife's name, or what the carrier of firewood means; the phrase can be read literally or figuratively.
- Not established: the occasion on which the passage was revealed; it names no event.
- Not established: what the rope of palm fibre signifies.
